utterances.text: Grandma Stiepel.
Who? What's my name?
Grandma Stiepel.
Grandma Stiepel? Here, let's turn the piano up. And you want to play piano for Grandma Stiepel? How old are you, Kaya?
12. Oh, that's pretty. So what I really need to do is get my hands— especially this hand is very— This finger is twisted because it's got arthritis in it, so I have to start using it.
Right, and it's good to play piano just for that purpose, just to use it, and just playing that 5 fingers.
Yeah, that will help a lot.

Right, and if you— that's a good exercise, Grandma. If you want to make that exercise even more extended a little— Uh-huh. Okay, so you see how— okay, here's how you play C, D, E, F, G, and then just move your hand up.
Oh, one more over.
One more over and do the same thing.
Oh, well, that's good exercise.
So that you can move up, and then when you come backwards, you can come backwards starting with pinky. Uh-huh.
Yeah, well, that's what I need is to get my hands limbered up.
Great. You want to try that?
Yeah.
Okay, then just move up. Just move up one.
Oh, just move up one?
Move your thumb. Thumb. And then start here now.
Oh.

Right, and then move up. Use yourself. Uh-huh. Right. There you go. Now you can go as high as you want, then start coming backwards. Start with your pinky, wherever you're at. And then move your pinky down one.
My pinky? Oh yeah, next time it's my pinky.
And then you won't get so bored just doing it in one spot.
Yeah.
You just travel up and down the piano.
I'll do that. I'll practice that a lot. Because then I think it's so much easier after you get your hands where you can move them.
Mm-hmm. It's a good warm-up. So for your right hand, and you can do the same thing with your left hand if you want to warm your left hand up. Same pattern, same way. And then just move up.
Just move the thumb up. No, this one, you have to start back here.
Right. And you know what that also does? It kind of gives you a little bit more familiarity with the rest of the piano.
It does.
Okay, so Grandma, show me the variation now of that where you play 2 on each one. 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2. Do you like that, Grandma?
Yeah.
Do you like it? You look like you're concentrating.
Yeah it's fun.
It is, isn't it? Yeah. Did I tell you what my new product is called? I'm calling it my 'Boot Camp' series.
Boot camp? Why on earth would you call it that? I'm not enlisting in the army, I'm just trying to play 'Mary Had a Little Lamb'!
Oh, no! hhhh It's just a name people use now for intense training sessions. You know, like a fitness class. I'm calling the specific one 'Boot Camp for Clumsy Fingers.'
Oh, that's funny hhhh. Well, as long as I don't have to do any push-ups on the keys!
